subject.title: Add a slim Docker image mode with configurable APT package installation

question: Should OpenClaw support deployer-configured APT packages for pulled official Docker images, and if so should the supported path be a derived-image prebuild flow instead of a startup-time installer?
rationale: The choice affects official image hardening, root package-manager execution, gateway downtime, env/CLI contract semantics, and constrained-host behavior, so code inspection cannot safely pick the product/security boundary.

options.title: Design derived-image prebuild flow
options.body: Keep this issue open and specify a prebuild command or documented Dockerfile.extend pattern that builds from the current official image before restarting the gateway.

options.title: Allow startup-time installer
options.body: Accept the downtime and package-manager risk by adding an explicit first-boot or entrypoint installer with caching, logging, and fail-loud semantics.

options.title: Keep build-time customization only
options.body: Close or defer this direction and continue steering operators to local/source image builds or custom Dockerfiles for extra packages.

recommendation.title: Design derived-image prebuild flow
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and specify a prebuild command or documented Dockerfile.extend pattern that builds from the current official image before restarting the gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the best available routing candidate from the original optional APT package merge and follow-up docs history for deciding whether the Docker env/CLI and security contract should expand beyond build-time customization.
